They drop forwards from the animation, so the spinner snaps back to opacity 0.
They omit role=status and an accessible label, so screen readers hear nothing.

Create the file status.html inside it.
Add a div with role='status' and aria-live='polite' that stays empty until loading finishes.

K-021116.check: grep -c prints 1, and npx axe reports zero violations for status.html.

Serve the built app on port 4173 in the background.
Run Lighthouse on the empty state route and save the JSON report.
Read the cumulative layout shift value from the report.

K-021128.check: jq prints a number at or below 0.1 and lh-empty.json exists.

steps.do: Count the lines that contain a th opening tag in the table component.
Count the lines that contain a scope attribute in the table component.
Count the lines that contain a caption opening tag in the table component.
Run the header test with Playwright and read the summary line.

K-021129.example: The file has 4 th lines and 4 lines with scope=, so every header is marked. The caption count is 1, which means one caption opening tag. Playwright ends with 'passed' and shows 0 failed, so the test agrees with the markup.
K-021129.check: The scope count equals the th count, the caption count is 1, and the Playwright run exits with code 0 and reports 0 failed.
traps: A caption count of 0 means the table has no caption, which is a real failure.
Missing scope on a th is a real failure even when the table looks right.
Count th lines only if each header sits on its own line, and do not count thead as a th.
Do not accept a passing look as proof; use the Playwright exit code and summary.

steps.do: Build the production bundle of the Vue app.
Start the preview server on port 4173 in its own terminal and leave it running.
Run the Lighthouse accessibility category against the users page and save a JSON report.
Read the accessibility score from the saved report.
Confirm the report file exists, then press Ctrl+C in the preview server terminal to stop it.

K-021130.example: The jq command prints 1 when Lighthouse scores the page at 100. A value such as 0.87 means the page has audit failures that need fixing before release.
K-021130.check: The jq output is 1, and the report file is listed by ls with exit code 0.
traps: A small model may score the dev server instead of the built preview, which gives different results.
Do not stop at a passing score without opening the report to see failed audits.
The score is a fraction from 0 to 1, not a percentage.

steps.do: Find where ratatui draw functions already live in the source tree.
Confirm the ratatui version in use so the plan matches its API.
Write in PLAN.md an enum AppState with exactly three variants: Loading, Empty, Ready.
Set the snapshot test size to 80 columns by 24 rows using TestBackend.

K-021131.example: The plan lists AppState as Loading, Empty, and Ready, and a snapshot test uses TestBackend::new(80, 24). The Empty variant renders a Paragraph inside a centered Block.
K-021131.check: cargo tree -i ratatui prints a line starting with ratatui v followed by a version number.
traps: Small models add a fourth variant such as Error, which the plan did not ask for.
Do not run cargo test in plan stage; there is no code to test yet.
TestBackend size must be written as columns then rows, 80 then 24.

steps.do: Read package.json to see if ink and ink-spinner are already listed as dependencies.
Search the source for Spinner usages that would show a loading state.
Write in PLAN.md that the spinner appears after 200ms of pending work and is hidden on resolve.

K-021132.example: package.json lists ink at version 5 and ink-spinner, so the plan keeps the spinner and sets its threshold to 200ms. The empty state is a Box with one Text line that reads No items yet.
K-021132.check: cat package.json shows ink and ink-spinner under dependencies.
traps: Small models invent ink-spinner when it is not listed; add it only in the build stage after the plan says so.
A threshold written as a word like short is not measurable; always write a number of ms.
Do not install packages during the plan stage.

steps.do: Search the code for getmaxyx to see where the screen size is read today.
Record in PLAN.md that the message row is height divided by 2 and the column is (width minus message length) divided by 2.
Record in PLAN.md that the screen needs at least 80 columns and 24 rows, and that q quits.
List the top-level files that would hold the curses code.

K-021133.example: On a 24-row, 80-column terminal the message 'No items yet' starts at row 12, column 34. The loading spinner uses the same row and column.
K-021133.check: rg -n getmaxyx . prints a line for each place the screen size is read, or no output if none exist yet.
traps: getmaxyx returns rows first, then columns, and small models often swap them.
Do not guess row values; compute them from 24 rows, which gives row 12.
The plan stops before any curses.wrapper call is written.

steps.do: Find existing Layout usage to match the constraint style already in the code.
Confirm the ratatui version so the plan uses the matching Constraint names.
Write in PLAN.md the vertical split as Percentage 40, Length 3, Percentage 60.
Write in PLAN.md that the message block is 3 rows tall and the layout must work at 80 by 24.

K-021134.example: The vertical split is Percentage 40 above, Length 3 for the message block, and Percentage 60 below, so on a 24-row screen the block starts at row 9 and ends at row 11. The Paragraph wraps inside the block with a 1-column margin.
K-021134.check: rg -n Layout src prints each Layout use with its line number, or nothing if none exist.
traps: Small models use Constraint::Length for all three rows, which breaks on small terminals.
The Percentage 40 and 60 values plus Length 3 must fit the screen height, so the plan must state the row total.
Do not start drawing code; the plan only fixes the numbers.

steps.do: Read the current list view before editing it.
Add a switch on loadState inside the NavigationStack, and for case .empty return ContentUnavailableView("No items", systemImage: "tray", description: Text("Create an item to see it here.")).

Run the UI test that checks the empty state.
Count the ContentUnavailableView uses in the sources.

K-021135.check: The test output shows 'Executed 2 tests, with 0 failures' and grep prints one line that contains ContentUnavailableView.

steps.do: Add a Button inside the failed case that shows Label("Try again", systemImage: "arrow.clockwise") and calls the reload function.
Apply .frame(minHeight: 44) to the button so its tap area is at least 44 points tall.
Confirm the minimum height is present in the source.
Run the UI test that asserts the retry button frame height.

K-021136.check: grep prints one line for NavErrorView.swift, and the test output shows 'Executed 1 test, with 0 failures'.

steps.do: In the load function, sleep for 200 milliseconds before setting loadState to loading, using Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(200)).
Confirm the 200 millisecond delay constant exists in the sources.
Run the test that checks the spinner appears only after the delay.

K-021137.example: ProgressView() is shown only when the fetch takes longer than milliseconds(200) in NavListView.swift:18. The grep command should print that one line.
K-021137.check: grep prints one matching line and the test output shows 'with 0 failures'.

steps.do: Create the test file ContrastTests.swift in the test folder.
Write a test that computes the contrast ratio of the error color against Color(.systemBackground) and asserts the ratio is at least 4.5.
Run the contrast test.

K-021138.example: The test asserts that the error text color has a ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the system background in light mode. A ratio of 3.9:1 fails the test and the color must be darkened.
K-021138.check: The test output shows 'Executed 1 test, with 0 failures' and the computed ratio is 4.5 or higher.
traps: Do not check only one appearance, because dark mode can drop the ratio below 4.5:1; test both light and dark.
Do not confuse 4.5:1 for normal text with 3:1 for large text, because a small model may pick the wrong threshold.

steps.do: Create an empty tokens.css file in the project root.
Add a :root block to tokens.css that defines --modal-title-size as 1.25rem, --modal-title-weight as 600, --modal-body-size as 1rem, and --modal-body-leading as 1.5.
Add a link element for tokens.css above the modal.css link in modal.html.
Count the modal token lines defined in tokens.css.

K-021139.example: The :root block in tokens.css sets --modal-body-size to 1rem, which is 16px at the default root size. Then .modal-body in modal.css uses font-size: var(--modal-body-size) and never a px value.
K-021139.check: grep -c prints 4 because tokens.css has exactly four --modal- token lines, and the browser devtools Computed panel shows font-size 16px for .modal-body.
traps: Px font sizes block user zoom and text scaling, so keep rem for every modal size token.
A token written without the leading -- or outside :root does not register, so var() silently falls back to the inherited value.

steps.do: In a second terminal, start a static server from the project folder on port 8080.
Confirm the server answers for modal.html before running axe.
Open modal.html and click the trigger button so the dialog is visible.
Run axe against the page with the WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 AA tag set.
Compute the contrast ratio for each text and surface token pair and record any pair below 4.5:1.

K-021140.example: Body text #1f1f1f on the surface token #ffffff gives about 16.5:1, which passes. Gray #9a9a9a on white gives about 2.8:1, which fails the 4.5:1 minimum and must be darkened.
K-021140.check: curl -I prints HTTP/1.1 200 OK, and axe reports 0 color-contrast violations for the open dialog.
traps: Axe only inspects rendered elements, so run it after the dialog opens.
Do not lower body text to 3:1 because it looks large, since only 18.66px bold or 24px text qualifies for 3:1.

steps.do: Confirm the spec file exists before running it.
Create tests/modal-type.spec.js that imports test and expect from @playwright/test.
In the test, open http://localhost:8080/modal.html and click the trigger button.
Add an expect that the computed font-size of .modal-body equals 16px.
Add an expect that the bounding box height of the close button is at least 44px.
Run the spec with the line reporter.

K-021141.example: The first expect checks 16px, the computed value of 1rem at a 16px root. The second expect checks a close button height of 44px or more, which meets the 44px touch target minimum.
K-021141.check: The line reporter ends with 2 passed and 0 failed, and the process exits with code 0.

Forgetting to start the server on port 8080 makes every test fail with net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED.

Replace each literal with the matching token, such as var(--modal-body-size) or var(--modal-text).
Re-run the same grep and confirm it prints no lines.
Run stylelint on modal.css to check declarations the grep cannot see.
Count the var token uses in modal.css as a positive signal.

K-021142.example: Before the fix, grep prints a line for font-size: 14px and another for color: #333. After replacing them with var(--modal-body-size) and var(--modal-text), the second grep exits with status 1 and prints nothing.
K-021142.check: The second grep exits with status 1 and no output, npx stylelint reports 0 problems, and the var(-- count is above 0.
traps: Grep exit status 1 means no matches, which is the pass state here, not an error.
Hex values inside var() fallbacks still count as literals, so read the fallbacks by hand.

steps.do: Add --modal-title-size to the :root block in tokens.css with the value clamp(1.125rem, 2.5vw + 0.75rem, 1.5rem).
Confirm the clamp token is defined exactly once in tokens.css.
Create tests/modal-clamp.spec.js that sets the viewport width to 320px, then 1280px, before reading .modal-title font-size.
Assert the title computed font-size is 20px at 320px and 24px at 1280px.
Run the viewport spec with the line reporter.

K-021143.example: At 320px wide, 2.5vw is 8px and 0.75rem is 12px, so the middle value is 20px, which sits between the 18px minimum and 24px maximum. At 1280px the middle value is 44px, which the clamp caps at 24px.
K-021143.check: grep -c prints 1, and the line reporter ends with 2 passed and 0 failed.
traps: Pure vw values ignore the user's browser font size, so always keep the rem term.
Testing only the minimum or maximum misses a broken middle formula, so also check a width between 320px and 1280px.

Create the state file NavLoadState.swift.

Count the font-size custom properties declared in the file.
Confirm the base size token is exactly 1rem and not a px value.

Run axe against the page with the wcag2aa tag and exit non-zero on violations.
Confirm no color-contrast violation appears, since body text needs at least 4.5:1 and large text at least 3:1.
